observations.note: The defended case is a justified threshold-and-equal-lottery allocation. A privacy claim alone does not produce a numerical entitlement. Correcting Ada's wrongful exclusion may reduce the other applicants from one-half to one-third; extra merit above the threshold gives no further credit. Conservation of probability only exposes a conflict after the rightful corrected baseline is established. Comparative merit schemes remain harder; inherited source access is openly limited.

The condition concerns whether a competent refusal can obtain its advertised operative consequence while the person remains in the relationship. It permits later persuasion, autonomous actual approval and even effective subsequent consent. A ratification may waive a debt but cannot establish that the institution previously surrendered discretion it retained. The concrete independent-review trigger distinguishes missing authority from merely bad labels, and the argument remains a diagnostic restriction on a particular defence rather than a universal theory of transformation.

Review requires information that can still arrive under the specific recommendation error being checked. A separate company using filtered summaries can fail; the same product with an unfiltered inbox can succeed. The manuscript distinguishes individual appeal from sampling a practice, and says a justified decision to surrender review does not establish its retention. It acknowledges meaningful-human-control and contestability precedents; proposed contribution is the failure-relative test plus task/timing distinctions.
